article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Marshmallow OG × Banana Butter Cups
Breeder: Square One Genetics
THC Content: 25-27%
CBD Content: Low
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Vanilla cream, gas, banana peel
Flowering Time (Indoor): 65–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: mid-October
Indoor Yield: Medium-heavy
Outdoor Yield: Medium-heavy
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Mello Nilla takes the idea of a vanilla-flavored cannabis strain in a direction that is considerably more complex than the name suggests. Sweet cream and soft floral notes may form the first impression, but underneath them sits a much heavier foundation of fuel, Kush, sour fruit, skunk, wood, and occasionally chocolate-like richness. That contrast comes directly from a pedigree pairing Compound Genetics’ Marshmallow OG with Square One Genetics’ Banana Butter Cups. Instead of producing another straightforward dessert hybrid, the cross layers creamy sweetness over some notably aggressive Chem, OG, diesel, and skunk ancestry.

Square One Genetics officially classifies Mello Nilla as an F1 feminized cross and describes its aromatic profile with four straightforward terms: gas, sweet, floral, and vanilla. The breeder lists flowering at 65–70 days and rates production as medium-heavy. Those specifications make the cultivar appealing to growers looking for premium dessert-style marijuana without sacrificing yield or the deeper fuel character that often disappears in sweeter modern hybrids.
Genetics and Lineage

Marshmallow OG supplies the gassy, creamy side of the family tree. The cultivar was bred by Compound Genetics from ( Chem D × Triangle Kush ) × Jet Fuel Gelato , a pedigree that brings together some of the most recognizable fuel-oriented cannabis lines of the modern era. Chem D contributes skunk, chemical funk, and diesel intensity; Triangle Kush reinforces earthy OG character and physical weight; Jet Fuel Gelato adds creamier sweetness and contemporary resin production. 710 Labs, which preserves Marshmallow OG in its genetics library, documents the same lineage and describes the cultivar’s aroma as musky, earthy, and sweet with a salted-caramel quality.

Banana Butter Cups pushes Mello Nilla in a stranger direction. Square One Genetics created that parent from the Loki Gro cut of Banana Punch crossed with PB & Jealous. Its official breeder profile lists banana peel, sour, woody, skunky, and chocolate characteristics rather than the simple banana-candy aroma its name might imply. PB & Jealous itself is documented by Square One as Oregon Raspberry × Peanut Butter Breath , contributing nutty, floral, and sweet qualities. When these traits meet Marshmallow OG, the resulting genetic palette becomes unusually broad: vanilla cream, ripe banana skin, flowers, chocolate, sourness, OG gas, and skunk can all compete for attention.

Because Mello Nilla is an F1, some phenotype variation should be expected. One plant may emphasize Marshmallow OG’s creamy fuel and vanilla character, while another may pull stronger banana, wood, skunk, or sour traits from Banana Butter Cups. That diversity can be valuable to growers hunting for a keeper, particularly when aroma and resin quality matter as much as raw yield.
Effects and Experience

Mello Nilla does not yet have enough breeder-backed consumer data to justify rigid claims about its effects, and Square One does not publish an official THC percentage. Its ancestry nevertheless points toward a potent modern hybrid experience rather than an especially light or purely energetic form of weed. Marshmallow OG selections are commonly associated with an initial euphoric mental shift followed by stronger physical relaxation, while Banana Butter Cups carries a blend of OG, Punch, Peanut Butter Breath, and fruit genetics capable of adding both cerebral engagement and body weight.

At moderate intake, the experience may begin with a noticeable improvement in mood and a softer, more comfortable mental state. The sweet aroma can make the onset feel deceptively approachable, but the Chem, Triangle Kush, Jet Fuel, and Punch ancestry provides considerable potential for the high to become heavier as it develops. Conversation, music, gaming, or watching a movie may fit the early phase particularly well before the body component becomes more apparent.

Larger amounts are more likely to emphasize physical relaxation, hazier concentration, and reduced motivation. Anyone trying a new batch should rely on the cannabinoid analysis printed on that specific product rather than an online strain-wide THC estimate. Potency can change dramatically with phenotype, cultivation environment, maturity at harvest, and laboratory methodology. Excessive THC can cause dry mouth, dizziness, short-term memory impairment, rapid heart rate, or anxiety in sensitive consumers.
Medical Benefits

Mello Nilla has not been evaluated in controlled clinical trials as an individual medical marijuana cultivar, so there is no evidence that the strain itself treats a specific disease. Its likely combination of mood elevation and later physical relaxation may nevertheless appeal to medical cannabis consumers who prefer THC-dominant hybrids for temporary stress relief, appetite support, discomfort, or help relaxing later in the day.

The cultivar may be particularly appealing to people who dislike cannabis that becomes immediately sedating. Depending on phenotype and dose, the experience can potentially retain a period of mental engagement before physical heaviness becomes more apparent. Higher doses may reverse that advantage by impairing attention or causing substantial lethargy, so patients with lower THC tolerance should approach potent flower conservatively.

Square One’s description of gas, floral, sweet, and vanilla traits refers primarily to sensory expression rather than a laboratory terpene panel. It would therefore be inaccurate to assign one universal dominant terpene to every Mello Nilla plant. Medical consumers interested in terpenes should consult the certificate of analysis for their actual batch rather than assuming that aroma alone establishes its chemical composition.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Vanilla is the defining sweet note, but Mello Nilla should not be mistaken for a soft vanilla-only strain. Fresh flowers may open with creamy sweetness, flowers, and a marshmallow-like quality before the heavier aromas underneath become apparent. Breaking the buds apart can release stronger fuel, skunk, earth, and sour notes, producing a contrast between bakery sweetness and the sharper marijuana funk inherited from Chem and OG genetics.

Banana Butter Cups adds another layer. Square One describes that parent with banana peel, sour, woody, skunky, and chocolate notes. In Mello Nilla, those characteristics can transform the sweeter profile into something resembling vanilla cream over ripe banana skin, woody spice, cocoa, and gasoline. The banana component is not necessarily a sugary banana-candy flavor; greener, slightly bitter peel notes may appear in phenotypes that lean strongly toward the paternal side.

On the palate, creamy vanilla and sweetness can arrive first, followed by flowers and mild fruit. Gas, earth, wood, and skunk become more noticeable on the exhale, while some expressions may leave a faint chocolate or nutty aftertaste. A careful cure should benefit this cultivar considerably, since excessive heat or overly rapid drying can flatten the floral and vanilla top notes and leave mostly fuel and earth behind.
Growing Information

Square One Genetics lists Mello Nilla at 65–70 days of flowering, placing the indoor cycle at roughly nine to ten weeks. The breeder rates yield as medium-heavy, a notable improvement over Banana Butter Cups itself, which Square One classifies as low-medium yielding. That suggests the Marshmallow OG pairing successfully adds production potential without requiring an unusually long flowering schedule.

Because the cultivar was released as a feminized F1, growers should still anticipate some structural differences between individual plants. Marshmallow OG-leaning phenotypes may show more OG-like stretch and dense resinous flowers, while Banana Butter Cups influence could alter internodal spacing, flower shape, color, and aroma. Topping or low-stress branch training during vegetative growth can help develop a broader canopy and make better use of available light.

Late flowering deserves careful environmental management. Heavy resin and increasingly dense flowers benefit from good airflow and moderate humidity, particularly when plants are packed closely together. Branch support may also become necessary on the more productive phenotypes as flowers gain weight. For growers hunting a keeper, yield alone should not determine selection. Aroma intensity, resin coverage, branch strength, flowering speed, and the balance between vanilla sweetness and pungent gas are all valuable traits to evaluate.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Mello Nilla?
Mello Nilla is Marshmallow OG × Banana Butter Cups. Square One Genetics officially lists the cultivar as a feminized F1.
Who bred the Mello Nilla strain?
Square One Genetics bred Mello Nilla. The strain was released as part of the breeder’s Banana Butter Cups-based work and is documented in Square One’s official cultivar archive.
What does Mello Nilla taste like?

The core profile combines vanilla, sweetness, flowers, and gas. Depending on phenotype, additional flavors can include banana peel, skunk, sour fruit, wood, chocolate, cream, earth, and OG-style fuel.
Is Mello Nilla indica or sativa?

Mello Nilla is best classified as a hybrid. Its pedigree combines heavy OG, Chem, Kush, Gelato, Punch, and Peanut Butter Breath influences, making a simple indica-or-sativa percentage less useful than describing its likely progression from cerebral uplift toward stronger physical relaxation.
How long does Mello Nilla take to flower?
Square One Genetics lists a flowering period of 65–70 days, or approximately nine to ten weeks indoors. The breeder rates its yield as medium-heavy.
Final Thoughts on Mello Nilla

Mello Nilla succeeds because the vanilla concept is only the beginning of its flavor profile. Marshmallow OG establishes a foundation of creamy sweetness, Chem funk, Kush, and fuel, while Banana Butter Cups introduces banana peel, flowers, sourness, wood, chocolate, and skunk. Together, those parents create marijuana capable of moving from dessert-like vanilla into considerably darker territory within the same flower.

The breeding also has practical appeal. A 65–70 day flowering period keeps the cycle manageable, while Square One’s medium-heavy yield rating gives the strain more production potential than many boutique dessert cultivars. The F1 structure leaves room for phenotype hunting, allowing growers to search for plants that emphasize vanilla cream, banana funk, heavy gas, floral sweetness, or some combination of all four.

For cannabis enthusiasts who enjoy sweet strains but find many modern dessert hybrids too predictable, Mello Nilla offers considerably more depth. Its strongest expressions should combine creamy vanilla and flowers with sour fruit, wood, skunk, chocolate, and old-fashioned fuel, giving the cultivar a distinctive identity that extends well beyond its playful name.
